To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Kirkwood-Buffs theory of solutions is useful for the development of new nonbonded parameters for carbohydrates and that these parameters can be used to calculate preferential interaction coefficients of carbohydrates and proteins that agree well with experimental data.

the CHARMM36 force field carbohydrate parameters do not reproduce the experimental thermodynamic data for carbohydrates, and that new parameters based on Kirkwood-Buff integrals are needed for accurate simulations of carbohydrates in solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new carbohydrate force field for molecular simulation and its application to the calculation of preferential interaction coefficients for aqueous carbohydrates and proteins.
understanding the molecular interactions that govern the thermodynamics of protein stabilization by excipients and the development of force fields that accurately reproduce the experimental data.
understanding the thermodynamic properties and molecular mechanisms of carbohydrate-protein interactions and how carbohydrates interact with each other in solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new carbohydrate parameters are superior to the CHARMM force field parameters in reproducing the thermodynamic properties and trends of carbohydrates, and thus should be used in simulations of carbohydrates in aqueous solution and in protein excipients.
the new carbohydrate parameters are more reliable in reproducing experimental data than the CHARMM36 parameter set.

the new carbohydrate parameters, developed using the Kirkwood-Buffs integral values, reproduce the experimental thermodynamic data for carbohydrates better than the CHARMM36 parameter set, and the preferential interaction coefficient calculations of carbohydrates with proteins using these parameters agree well with experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new carbohydrate parameters reproduce the experimental data for carbohydrate self-association, carbohydrate-water interactions, and carbohydrate-protein interactions.
the Kirkwood-Buffs integral values are a useful tool for the development and testing of force field parameters for carbohydrates and their application to protein-carbohydrate simulations.

the CHARMM36 parameter set for carbohydrates is unsuitable for simulations of carbohydrate-protein solutions, and the Kirkwood-Buffs-derived carbohydrate parameters should be used for simulations of carbohydrate interactions with proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kirkwood-Buffs theory of solutions is useful for developing force fields for carbohydrates and other solutes that can be applied to simulations of excipient-protein interactions.
it is necessary to have a force field that reproduces experimental thermodynamic data in order to accurately calculate preferential interaction coefficients.
force fields for carbohydrates should be developed to reproduce experimental trends in thermodynamic properties of carbohydrate-water and carbohydrate-protein systems.
